photoobj_star_cohort.name: photoobj_star_cohort
photoobj_star_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  -- canonicalized is_clean indicator: treat any nonzero clean as 1, zero or NULL as 0
  CASE WHEN p.clean IS NOT NULL AND p.clean <> 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS clean,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM photoobj p
JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'STAR'

semantic_filters.clean IS NOT NULL: rows where photoobj.clean is not NULL

photoobj_star_cohort.description: Row-level cohort of photoobj rows that represent photometrically-classified stars (photoobj.type matches the photo_type.name = 'STAR' mapping). Exposes identifying, positional and photometric columns for each photo object and a canonicalized 'is_clean' indicator.

photoobj_photometry_normalized.name: photoobj_photometry_normalized
photoobj_photometry_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key
  objid,

  -- basic identifiers & flags (cast to exact types)
  run::smallint  AS run,
  rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  field::smallint AS field,
  mode::smallint  AS mode,
  type::integer   AS type,
  clean::integer  AS clean,

  -- photometry: keep as real (float4) and treat impossible sentinel values as NULL.
  -- lift question-specific sentinel literals out: sentinel_mag = -9999
  (CASE WHEN u IS NULL OR u = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE u::real END) AS u,
  (CASE WHEN g IS NULL OR g = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE g::real END) AS g,
  (CASE WHEN r IS NULL OR r = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE r::real END) AS r,
  (CASE WHEN i IS NULL OR i = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE i::real END) AS i,
  (CASE WHEN z IS NULL OR z = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE z::real END) AS z,

  -- positions: RA/Dec as double precision; treat out-of-range as NULL
  (CASE WHEN ra IS NULL OR ra < 0 OR ra >= 360 THEN NULL ELSE ra::double precision END) AS ra,
  (CASE WHEN dec IS NULL OR dec < -90 OR dec > 90 THEN NULL ELSE dec::double precision END) AS dec,

  -- cmodel mags: canonical null handling using same sentinel
  (CASE WHEN cmodelmag_u IS NULL OR cmodelmag_u = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE cmodelmag_u::real END) AS cmodelmag_u,
  (CASE WHEN cmodelmag_g IS NULL OR cmodelmag_g = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE cmodelmag_g::real END) AS cmodelmag_g,
  (CASE WHEN cmodelmag_r IS NULL OR cmodelmag_r = -9999 THEN NULL ELSE cmodelmag_r::real END) AS cmodelmag_r,

  -- centroid columns as real, preserve NULLs
  (CASE WHEN rowc IS NULL OR rowc = 'Infinity'::real OR rowc = '-Infinity'::real THEN NULL ELSE rowc::real END) AS rowc,
  (CASE WHEN colc IS NULL OR colc = 'Infinity'::real OR colc = '-Infinity'::real THEN NULL ELSE colc::real END) AS colc,

  -- extinction_r: non-negative real or NULL
  (CASE WHEN extinction_r IS NULL OR extinction_r < 0 THEN NULL ELSE extinction_r::real END) AS extinction_r

FROM photoobj

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filtering; this view only projects and canonicalizes columns for reuse

photoobj_photometry_normalized.description: Normalized/photo-cleaned projection of photoobj photometric and positional columns with canonical null-handling and typed casts where appropriate. Keeps one row per photoobj.objid and includes the raw type code for joining to photo_type descriptions later.

photo_type_lookup.name: photo_type_lookup
photo_type_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM
  photo_type

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filtering; full code-to-name mapping

photo_type_lookup.description: Lookup table mapping photo_type.value (integer code) to human-readable name and description. Useful to translate photoobj.type codes to semantic labels such as 'STAR'.

photoobj_star_cohort_3.name: photoobj_star_cohort_3
photoobj_star_cohort_3.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion
FROM photoobj p
-- require photometrically usable detection
WHERE p.clean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean <> 0
-- require valid sky coordinates
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
-- require at least one measured magnitude (u/g/r/i/z)
  AND (
    p.u IS NOT NULL
    OR p.g IS NOT NULL
    OR p.r IS NOT NULL
    OR p.i IS NOT NULL
    OR p.z IS NOT NULL
  )

semantic_filters.at_least_one_mag: (u IS NOT NULL OR g IS NOT NULL OR r IS NOT NULL OR i IS NOT NULL OR z IS NOT NULL)

photoobj_star_cohort_3.description: Subset of photoobj rows that are photometrically usable detections (clean) and have non-null sky coordinates and at least one measured magnitude; intended to represent objects observable in imaging surveys. Does NOT bake the literal photo_type name for 'star' — that is left to question_ops.

photo_type_lookup_4.name: photo_type_lookup_4
photo_type_lookup_4.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM
  photo_type
photo_type_lookup_4.description: Canonical lookup of photo type codes to names/descriptions. Useful for joining/ filtering by human-readable object types (e.g., 'star', 'galaxy').

photoobj_core.name: photoobj_core
photoobj_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- normalize ra/dec: prefer normalized photometry view if available, else fallback to base photoobj
  COALESCE(pn.ra, p.ra) AS ra,
  COALESCE(pn.dec, p.dec) AS dec,
  -- type/run/rerun/field/mode are canonical from the photoobj table; if normalized view provides them prefer that
  COALESCE(pn.type, p.type) AS type,
  COALESCE(pn.run, p.run) AS run,
  COALESCE(pn.rerun, p.rerun) AS rerun,
  COALESCE(pn.field, p.field) AS field,
  COALESCE(pn.mode, p.mode) AS mode
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photoobj_photometry_normalized AS pn USING (objid)
photoobj_core.description: Canonical photo objects with key identifying columns and primary positional/photometric fields; preserves one row per photoobj.objid and normalizes nullable coords/photometry.

photo_type_lookup_6.name: photo_type_lookup_6
photo_type_lookup_6.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM photo_type
ORDER BY value
photo_type_lookup_6.description: Lookup of photo type codes to canonical names and descriptions; one row per photo_type.value.
validated_on: Show me the object id, right ascension, and declination of photometrically observed star that have spectral observations.

photoobj_with_spec_presence.name: photoobj_with_spec_presence
photoobj_with_spec_presence.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  (CASE WHEN s.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END) AS has_spec
FROM
  photoobj_core p
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT 1 AS specobjid
  FROM specobj s
  WHERE s.bestobjid = p.objid OR s.specobjid = p.objid
  LIMIT 1
) s ON true
photoobj_with_spec_presence.description: Photo objects annotated with a boolean indicating presence of any matching spectroscopic record. Matches when photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid OR photoobj.objid = specobj.specobjid. One row per photoobj.objid.

photoobj_with_specobj_links.name: photoobj_with_specobj_links
photoobj_with_specobj_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS photo_objid,
  p.ra AS photo_ra,
  p.dec AS photo_dec,
  p.type AS photo_type,
  s.specobjid AS spec_specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS spec_bestobjid,
  s.class AS spec_class,
  s.subclass AS spec_subclass
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
UNION ALL
SELECT
  p2.objid AS photo_objid,
  p2.ra AS photo_ra,
  p2.dec AS photo_dec,
  p2.type AS photo_type,
  s2.specobjid AS spec_specobjid,
  s2.bestobjid AS spec_bestobjid,
  s2.class AS spec_class,
  s2.subclass AS spec_subclass
FROM photoobj p2
JOIN specobj s2
  ON p2.objid = s2.specobjid
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM specobj s3 WHERE s3.bestobjid = p2.objid
  )
photoobj_with_specobj_links.description: Denormalized relation linking photoobj rows to matching specobj rows when a spectral observation exists, exposing both link keys so queries can prefer specobj.bestobjid or specobj.specobjid.

specobj_bestobjid_cohort.name: specobj_bestobjid_cohort
specobj_bestobjid_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.bestobjid,
  s.specobjid,
  s.plateid,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.class,
  s.subclass
FROM specobj s
-- Restrict to spectroscopically observed objects: those with a bestobjid present.
-- Optionally restrict to specobj rows that also appear in galaxy spectroscopic tables:
-- lift the filter literal OUT so callers can control whether to apply it.
-- To restrict to galspecline set the parameter 'include_only_galaxy_spec' = 'true'
-- (not enforced inside the view); here we include all specobj rows that have a non-null bestobjid.
WHERE s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
-- Ensure unique row per bestobjid: keep the first specobj row per bestobjid by minimal specobjid.
AND s.specobjid = (
  SELECT MIN(s2.specobjid)
  FROM specobj s2
  WHERE s2.bestobjid = s.bestobjid
)
specobj_bestobjid_cohort.description: Cohort of specobj bestobjid values for spectroscopically observed objects, optionally restricted to those specobjids that appear in spectroscopic galaxy tables like galspecline or spplines. One row per specobj.bestobjid.

spectroscopic_objects.name: spectroscopic_objects
spectroscopic_objects.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.ra::double precision AS spec_ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS spec_dec,
  s.z::real AS redshift,
  s.class::varchar AS class,
  s.subclass::varchar AS subclass,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid
FROM specobj s
spectroscopic_objects.description: Cohort of spectroscopic observations (one row per specobj) with key spectroscopic fields normalized for reuse.

photo_objects_nonnull_photom.name: photo_objects_nonnull_photom
photo_objects_nonnull_photom.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.type,
  p.run,
  p.field,
  p.rerun
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
WHERE
  -- positional columns must be present
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- required photometric magnitudes must be present
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  -- required metadata for joins
  AND p.extinction_r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.type IS NOT NULL
  AND p.run IS NOT NULL
  AND p.field IS NOT NULL
  AND p.rerun IS NOT NULL
photo_objects_nonnull_photom.description: Photometric detections with required positional and photometric columns present (one row per photoobj). Excludes rows with NULL positional or magnitude values to support joins that require complete photometry.

specobj_photoobj_join_by_bestobjid.name: specobj_photoobj_join_by_bestobjid
specobj_photoobj_join_by_bestobjid.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.ra::double precision AS spec_ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS spec_dec,
  s.z::real AS redshift,
  p.objid::bigint AS photo_objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS photo_ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS photo_dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.extinction_r::real AS extinction_r
FROM specobj s
JOIN photoobj p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
WHERE
  -- require non-null/finite spectro coords and redshift
  s.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND s.dec IS NOT NULL
  AND s.z IS NOT NULL
  -- require complete photometry (lifted literals: 'required_phot_cols' conceptually)
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.photo_photometry_nonnull: photoobj.u, photoobj.g, photoobj.r, photoobj.i, photoobj.z, photoobj.ra, photoobj.dec NOT NULL

specobj_photoobj_join_by_bestobjid.description: Denormalized view joining spectroscopic objects to their matched photometric detection via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. One row per spectroscopic object that has a matching photoobj and complete photometry.

photo_objects_normalized.name: photo_objects_normalized
photo_objects_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- NULL-clean RA/DEC: prefer photoobj ra/dec, but coerce extreme out-of-range or NULL to NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN p.ra IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.ra < -360 OR p.ra > 360 THEN NULL
    ELSE p.ra
  END AS ra,
  CASE
    WHEN p.dec IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.dec < -90 OR p.dec > 90 THEN NULL
    ELSE p.dec
  END AS dec,
  p.type,
  p.run,
  p.field,
  -- normalize clean to integer NULL or value; carry through as-is from photoobj core/cohort source
  p.clean
FROM
  -- prefer the canonical photoobj_core when available (it provides core identification + astrometry),
  -- otherwise fall back to photoobj_photometry_normalized, then photoobj_star_cohort.
  -- Use COALESCE-style priority by LEFT JOIN chain to pick first non-null objid source.
  (
    SELECT
      co.objid,
      co.ra,
      co.dec,
      co.type,
      co.run,
      co.field,
      -- photoobj_core doesn't expose clean; join to photometry normalized to fetch clean if possible
      pn.clean
    FROM photoobj_core co
    LEFT JOIN photoobj_photometry_normalized pn ON pn.objid = co.objid

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      pn2.objid,
      pn2.ra,
      pn2.dec,
      pn2.type,
      pn2.run,
      pn2.field,
      pn2.clean
    FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized pn2
    WHERE pn2.objid NOT IN (SELECT objid FROM photoobj_core)

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      sc.objid,
      sc.ra,
      sc.dec,
      sc.type,
      sc.run,
      sc.field,
      sc.clean
    FROM photoobj_star_cohort sc
    WHERE sc.objid NOT IN (SELECT objid FROM photoobj_core)
      AND sc.objid NOT IN (SELECT objid FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized)
  ) p

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; all photoobj rows are exposed (NULL ra/dec preserved but can be filtered later)

photo_objects_normalized.description: Canonical photoobj rows with essential identification, astrometry, phototype id, and NULL-cleaned RA/DEC for reuse in joins and filters.

spectroscopic_to_photo_link.name: spectroscopic_to_photo_link
spectroscopic_to_photo_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric                     AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint                       AS bestobjid,
  COALESCE(p.ra, p2.ra)                     AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, p2.dec)                   AS dec,
  s.class                                   AS class,
  s.z::real                                 AS z,
  s.mjd                                     AS mjd
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
LEFT JOIN photoobj p2
  ON p2.objid = s.specobjid::bigint

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; exposes all specobj rows and their photo linkage columns

spectroscopic_to_photo_link.description: Denormalized mapping of spectroscopic records to photometric object ids using both specobj.bestobjid and specobj.specobjid to allow linking either way.

photo_type_lookup_15.name: photo_type_lookup_15
photo_type_lookup_15.body_sql:

photo_type_lookup_15.description: Lookup of photo_type value to canonical name and description to interpret photoobj.type codes (e.g., 'GALAXY').

photoobj_primary_clean_positions.name: photoobj_primary_clean_positions
photoobj_primary_clean_positions.body_sql:

WHERE p.clean = 1

  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
photoobj_primary_clean_positions.description: Photometric detections that are primary/clean suitable for scientific analysis, exposing identifiers and sky positions.

specobj_classification.name: specobj_classification
specobj_classification.body_sql:

photo_with_spec_join.name: photo_with_spec_join
photo_with_spec_join.body_sql:
SELECT

photo_with_spec_join.description: Denormalized join of photometric detections to their associated spectroscopic observations via photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid, exposing both photo and spec keys and key classification fields for downstream filtering.

specobj_base.name: specobj_base
specobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT

specobj_base.description: Canonical projection of spectroscopic objects (specobj) exposing identifiers, sky position and redshift/classification fields for joining to photometric objects or for selection by spectroscopic properties.

photoobj_neighbors.name: photoobj_neighbors
photoobj_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,

  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,

FROM

photoobj_neighbors.description: Pairs of a photometric object and its neighbor from the neighbors table, exposing distances, neighbor id and neighbor types for spatial/cohort neighbor queries and isolation checks.

photometric_objects_core.name: photometric_objects_core
photometric_objects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  -- lift photometry literals out: prefer normalized photometry when available, fall back to raw
  COALESCE(ppn.u, p.u) AS u,
  COALESCE(ppn.g, p.g) AS g,
  COALESCE(ppn.r, p.r) AS r,
  COALESCE(ppn.i, p.i) AS i,
  COALESCE(ppn.z, p.z) AS z,
  -- lift positional/run fields out: prefer photoobj_core when present to ensure canonical run/field/rerun/mode
  COALESCE(pc.run, p.run) AS run,
  COALESCE(pc.field, p.field) AS field,
  COALESCE(pc.rerun, p.rerun) AS rerun,
  COALESCE(pc.mode, p.mode) AS mode,
  -- clean flag: prefer normalized source then raw
  COALESCE(ppn.clean, p.clean) AS clean
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photoobj_photometry_normalized ppn ON ppn.objid = p.objid
LEFT JOIN photoobj_core pc ON pc.objid = p.objid
photometric_objects_core.description: Canonical photometric objects with raw positional and photometric columns normalized/selected for downstream filtering and joins. Does not apply any spatial or type filter so it can be reused for many queries.

photo_type_lookup_22.name: photo_type_lookup_22
photo_type_lookup_22.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name,
  pt.description
FROM
  photo_type pt
photo_type_lookup_22.description: Lookup table mapping photoobj.type integer codes to their semantic names and descriptions from photo_type. Useful to translate type codes into labels like 'GALAXY'.

photoobj_with_type_label.name: photoobj_with_type_label
photoobj_with_type_label.body_sql:

FROM

LEFT JOIN

ON

photoobj_with_type_label.description: Denormalized photometric objects joined to their photo_type label so queries can filter by human-readable type (e.g., 'GALAXY'). One row per photometric object with type name exposed.

photoobj_star_rows.name: photoobj_star_rows
photoobj_star_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.type::integer AS type,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.clean::integer AS clean
FROM photoobj_star_cohort AS p
photoobj_star_rows.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections that represent astronomical sources of a given photo type (stars). Filters that identify 'star' type are left to question_ops so the view can be reused for other photo types; includes positional and basic photometric/metadata columns.

photo_type_mapping.name: photo_type_mapping
photo_type_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,

photoobj_pos_and_photometry.name: photoobj_pos_and_photometry
photoobj_pos_and_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  COALESCE(p.ra, ppn.ra) AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, ppn.dec) AS dec,
  -- canonicalized magnitudes: prefer normalized photometry, fall back to raw photoobj cols
  COALESCE(ppn.u, p.u) AS u,
  COALESCE(ppn.g, p.g) AS g,
  COALESCE(ppn.r, p.r) AS r,
  COALESCE(ppn.i, p.i) AS i,
  COALESCE(ppn.z, p.z) AS z,
  COALESCE(ppn.cmodelmag_u, p.cmodelmag_u) AS cmodelmag_u,
  COALESCE(ppn.cmodelmag_g, p.cmodelmag_g) AS cmodelmag_g,
  COALESCE(ppn.cmodelmag_r, p.cmodelmag_r) AS cmodelmag_r,
  COALESCE(ppn.extinction_r, p.extinction_r) AS extinction_r,
  -- canonical clean flag: prefer normalized photometry, then star cohort, then raw
  COALESCE(ppn.clean, p.clean, psc.clean) AS clean,
  -- canonical type: prefer core/type-normalized, then normalized photometry, then raw
  COALESCE(pc.type, ppn.type, p.type) AS type
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photoobj_photometry_normalized ppn
  ON ppn.objid = p.objid
LEFT JOIN photoobj_core pc
  ON pc.objid = p.objid
LEFT JOIN photoobj_star_cohort psc
  ON psc.objid = p.objid
photoobj_pos_and_photometry.description: Canonicalized projection of photoobj with positions, canonical photometry, and basic quality flag so queries can uniformly reference RA/DEC and magnitudes; leaves cleaning/thresholding to question_ops.

photoobj_point_observations.name: photoobj_point_observations
photoobj_point_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- ensure RA/Dec are numeric double precision; lift any literals out (none required)
  CASE
    WHEN p.ra IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.ra::double precision
  END AS ra,
  CASE
    WHEN p.dec IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.dec::double precision
  END AS dec
FROM
  -- prefer canonical core if available for consistent positions; fall back to normalized photometry,
  -- then to star cohort. Carry objid through.
  photoobj_core p
UNION ALL
SELECT
  p.objid,
  CASE WHEN p.ra IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.ra::double precision END AS ra,
  CASE WHEN p.dec IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.dec::double precision END AS dec
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM photoobj_core c WHERE c.objid = p.objid)
UNION ALL
SELECT
  p.objid,
  CASE WHEN p.ra IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.ra::double precision END AS ra,
  CASE WHEN p.dec IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.dec::double precision END AS dec
FROM photoobj_star_cohort p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM photoobj_core c WHERE c.objid = p.objid)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized n WHERE n.objid = p.objid)

semantic_filters.None: This view does not apply question-specific value filters. It may include generic cleaning such as excluding NULL objid rows if present.

photoobj_point_observations.description: Canonical row-level representation of photometrically observed objects (one row per detected photo object) with core positional and photometric attributes, cleaned/cast as needed for downstream spatial or classification filters.

photo_type_lookup_28.name: photo_type_lookup_28
photo_type_lookup_28.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM photo_type pt

semantic_filters.None: No intrinsic filters; preserves all photo_type rows.

photo_type_lookup_28.description: Lookup table mapping numeric photoobj.type values to human-readable type names and descriptions. Useful for filtering objects by semantic types like 'STAR'.

photoobj_with_type.name: photoobj_with_type
photoobj_with_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value

semantic_filters.None: No intrinsic filters applied; join preserves all photoobj rows and matches photo_type when available.

photoobj_with_type.description: Denormalized view joining photoobj to photo_type to provide object rows annotated with the human-readable type name; one row per photoobj.objid.

spectroscopic_objects_30.name: spectroscopic_objects_30
spectroscopic_objects_30.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.class::varchar AS class,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid
FROM specobj s
spectroscopic_objects_30.description: One row per spectroscopic observation (specobj). Exposes primary identifying and positional columns and spectroscopic classification to form cohorts of spectroscopic objects.

specobj_with_photo_type.name: specobj_with_photo_type
specobj_with_photo_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.ra AS "specobj.ra",
  s.dec AS "specobj.dec",
  pt.name AS photo_type
FROM
  specobj s
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj p
ON
  s.bestobjid = p.objid
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
specobj_with_photo_type.description: Denormalized mapping of spectroscopic observations to their matched photometric object and photometric type. One row per specobj, joined to photoobj via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid.

photoobj_point_positions.name: photoobj_point_positions
photoobj_point_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_point_positions.description: Canonical per-object sky positions and basic identifying columns from the imaging catalog. Normalizes/renames raw photoobj coordinate and id columns for reuse in spatial and cross-match queries.

specobj_primary_classification.name: specobj_primary_classification
specobj_primary_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid
FROM specobj s
specobj_primary_classification.description: Per-spectrum canonical spectroscopic identification and linking key to the best-matching imaging object. Exposes spectroscopic redshift and classification flags for downstream filtering.

photoobj_with_spec_join.name: photoobj_with_spec_join
photoobj_with_spec_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS "photoobj.objid",
  p.ra AS "photoobj.ra",
  p.dec AS "photoobj.dec",
  s.specobjid AS "specobj.specobjid",
  s.z AS "specobj.z",
  s.class AS "specobj.class"
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_spec_join.description: Denormalized one-row-per-photoobj joined to its linked spectroscopic observation (if any). Useful for queries that need imaging positions together with spectroscopic properties.

specobj_rows.name: specobj_rows
specobj_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobj.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  specobj.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  specobj.plateid::numeric AS plateid,
  specobj.scienceprimary::smallint AS scienceprimary,
  specobj.segue2primary::smallint AS segue2primary,
  specobj.survey::character varying AS survey,
  specobj.programname::character varying AS programname,
  specobj.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  specobj.plate::smallint AS plate,
  specobj.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid,
  specobj.special_target1::bigint AS special_target1,
  specobj.segue2_target1::bigint AS segue2_target1,
  specobj.segue2_target2::bigint AS segue2_target2,
  specobj.ancillary_target1::bigint AS ancillary_target1,
  specobj.ra::double precision AS ra,
  specobj.dec::double precision AS dec,
  specobj.z::real AS z,
  specobj.zerr::real AS zerr,
  specobj.zwarning::integer AS zwarning,
  specobj.class::character varying AS class,
  specobj.subclass::character varying AS subclass,
  specobj.veldisp::real AS veldisp,
  specobj.veldisperr::real AS veldisperr,
  specobj.loadversion::integer AS loadversion
FROM specobj AS specobj
specobj_rows.description: Base row-level view of spectroscopic observation records (specobj table) exposing all native columns for filtering and joining. No domain-specific literals baked in.

photoobj_rows.name: photoobj_rows
photoobj_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.b,
  p.l,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_rows.description: Base row-level view of photometric object records (photoobj table) exposing all native columns for filtering and joining. Kept raw to allow spatial and photometric filters.
validated_on: Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2

specobj_with_photoobj.name: specobj_with_photoobj
specobj_with_photoobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobj.specobjid AS "specobj.specobjid",
  specobj.bestobjid AS "specobj.bestobjid",
  specobj.plateid AS "specobj.plateid",
  specobj.scienceprimary AS "specobj.scienceprimary",
  specobj.segue2primary AS "specobj.segue2primary",
  specobj.survey AS "specobj.survey",
  specobj.programname AS "specobj.programname",
  specobj.mjd AS "specobj.mjd",
  specobj.plate AS "specobj.plate",
  specobj.fiberid AS "specobj.fiberid",
  specobj.special_target1 AS "specobj.special_target1",
  specobj.segue2_target1 AS "specobj.segue2_target1",
  specobj.segue2_target2 AS "specobj.segue2_target2",
  specobj.ancillary_target1 AS "specobj.ancillary_target1",
  specobj.ra AS "specobj.ra",
  specobj.dec AS "specobj.dec",
  specobj.z AS "specobj.z",
  specobj.zerr AS "specobj.zerr",
  specobj.zwarning AS "specobj.zwarning",
  specobj.class AS "specobj.class",
  specobj.subclass AS "specobj.subclass",
  specobj.veldisp AS "specobj.veldisp",
  specobj.veldisperr AS "specobj.veldisperr",
  specobj.loadversion AS "specobj.loadversion",
  photoobj.objid AS "photoobj.objid",
  photoobj.run AS "photoobj.run",
  photoobj.rerun AS "photoobj.rerun",
  photoobj.field AS "photoobj.field",
  photoobj.mode AS "photoobj.mode",
  photoobj.type AS "photoobj.type",
  photoobj.clean AS "photoobj.clean",
  photoobj.flags AS "photoobj.flags",
  photoobj.rowc AS "photoobj.rowc",
  photoobj.colc AS "photoobj.colc",
  photoobj.cmodelmag_u AS "photoobj.cmodelmag_u",
  photoobj.cmodelmag_g AS "photoobj.cmodelmag_g",
  photoobj.cmodelmag_r AS "photoobj.cmodelmag_r",
  photoobj.ra AS "photoobj.ra",
  photoobj.dec AS "photoobj.dec",
  photoobj.b AS "photoobj.b",
  photoobj.l AS "photoobj.l",
  photoobj.extinction_r AS "photoobj.extinction_r",
  photoobj.mjd AS "photoobj.mjd",
  photoobj.loadversion AS "photoobj.loadversion",
  photoobj.u AS "photoobj.u",
  photoobj.g AS "photoobj.g",
  photoobj.r AS "photoobj.r",
  photoobj.i AS "photoobj.i",
  photoobj.z AS "photoobj.z"
FROM
  specobj
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj
ON
  specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid
specobj_with_photoobj.description: Denormalized one-row-per-specobj view joining specobj to its matched photometric record via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. Exposes all columns from both tables so downstream queries can filter on spectroscopic class and spatial bounds and return combined properties.

photoobj_core_positions.name: photoobj_core_positions
photoobj_core_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM photoobj p
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
photoobj_core_positions.description: Canonicalized photometric object positions and basic identifiers from the photoobj table. Prefer photo coordinates and expose necessary columns for spatial filtering and joins to spectroscopic records.

specobj_core_spectra.name: specobj_core_spectra
specobj_core_spectra.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.z::real AS z
FROM specobj s
specobj_core_spectra.description: Canonicalized spectroscopic observations and identifiers from specobj. Exposes spectroscopic redshift and coordinates; one row per spectroscopic observation.

photoobj_with_spec_link.name: photoobj_with_spec_link
photoobj_with_spec_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::bigint AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  s.z AS z
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_with_spec_link.description: Denormalized mapping of photometric objects to their linked spectroscopic records via specobj.bestobjid, exposing photo coordinates when available and spectroscopic redshift. One row per spectroscopic observation (specobjid) joined to its photoobj if present.

photoobj_star_canonical_mags.name: photoobj_star_canonical_mags
photoobj_star_canonical_mags.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- cast mags to real as requested (lift literals none)
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name
FROM
  -- prefer existing cohort view that already has star selection and mags/positions
  photoobj_star_cohort AS p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type_lookup AS pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
photoobj_star_canonical_mags.description: Per-photometric-object canonical record joining photoobj with photo_type to resolve type names; casts mags to real and exposes raw model magnitudes and positional/identifying columns for downstream filtering.

photoobj_star_color_indices.name: photoobj_star_color_indices
photoobj_star_color_indices.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z
FROM photoobj_star_cohort p
WHERE p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_color_indices.description: Per-photoobj computed color indices (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) for objects classified as stars. Keeps one row per photoobj and leaves numeric color columns for threshold filtering.

photoobj_basic_meta.name: photoobj_basic_meta
photoobj_basic_meta.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.run AS run,
  p.rerun AS rerun,
  p.field AS field,
  p.mode AS mode,
  p.type AS type,
  p.clean AS clean,
  -- lift raw flags literal out of view: callers may override by joining a flags source;
  -- here we pass through flags when available, otherwise NULL
  p.flags AS flags,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec
FROM
  -- prefer the most canonical/core projection when available: photoobj_core has minimal canonical columns
  -- fall back to photoobj_photometry_normalized or photoobj_star_cohort_3 which include flags/clean when present.
  -- Use COALESCE-style precedence via LEFT JOINs to preserve objid grain and carry through key columns.
  photoobj_core pc
  LEFT JOIN photoobj_photometry_normalized ppn USING (objid)
  LEFT JOIN photoobj_star_cohort_3 psc3 USING (objid)
  LEFT JOIN photoobj_star_cohort psc USING (objid)
  LEFT JOIN photoobj p ON p.objid = pc.objid
-- choose column precedence: prefer ppn, then psc3, then psc, then raw photoobj p, then core pc
-- implement precedence in SELECT by coalescing across joined sources
photoobj_basic_meta.description: Normalized per-photoobj metadata and common flags: exposes canonical id, survey positioning, run/rerun/field/mode/type, clean and raw flags, and ra/dec. Intended as a reusable projection for any query needing core photoobj columns.

photoobj_star_photometry_row.name: photoobj_star_photometry_row
photoobj_star_photometry_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj_star_cohort AS p
WHERE
  -- require all five PSF/aperture magnitudes present (lifted literals)
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_photometry_row.description: Photometric detections (one row per photometric object) restricted to rows that have all five band magnitudes present and correspond to photometric stars. Keeps raw magnitudes and positional + basic catalog columns to support color-based selection and joins.

photoobj_basic_canonical.name: photoobj_basic_canonical
photoobj_basic_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.run::integer AS run,
  p.rerun::integer AS rerun,
  p.field::integer AS field,
  p.mode::smallint AS mode,
  p.type::smallint AS type,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  -- canonical positions as double precision
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  -- broadband magnitudes preserved as real (nullable)
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  -- cmodel magnitudes (preserve as real)
  p.cmodelmag_u::real AS cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g::real AS cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r::real AS cmodelmag_r,
  -- extinction and centroid columns
  p.extinction_r::real AS extinction_r,
  p.rowc::real AS rowc,
  p.colc::real AS colc
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_basic_canonical.description: Canonicalized projection of photoobj with cleaned numeric types and canonical column names for magnitudes and positions. Useful as a normalized input to color calculations, joins, and downstream aggregations. Does not apply astrophysical cuts; preserves all rows (except none for missing mags are kept as NULL).

photoobj_neighbor_counts_by_obj.name: photoobj_neighbor_counts_by_obj
photoobj_neighbor_counts_by_obj.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  COUNT(n.neighborobjid) AS neighbor_count,
  MIN(n.distance) AS min_neighbor_distance,
  MAX(n.distance) AS max_neighbor_distance,
  AVG(n.distance) AS avg_neighbor_distance
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  neighbors n
  ON n.objid = p.objid
GROUP BY
  p.objid
photoobj_neighbor_counts_by_obj.description: Per-photoobj neighbor counts and nearest-neighbor distance summary (one row per photoobj.objid). Useful to flag isolated objects or blends; supports queries that may want to exclude objects with nearby neighbors or examine neighbor density.

photoobj_photometry_normalized_47.name: photoobj_photometry_normalized_47
photoobj_photometry_normalized_47.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj AS p
WHERE
  -- filter out any rows with NULL magnitudes so color calculations are simple downstream
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_photometry_normalized_47.description: Canonical projection of photoobj rows exposing identifying columns, positions, and raw band magnitudes; filters out rows with any NULL magnitudes to simplify color calculations.

neighbors_within_distance.name: neighbors_within_distance
neighbors_within_distance.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
WHERE
  n.distance <= /*{max_distance}*/ 1.0
  AND n.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL
neighbors_within_distance.description: Subset of neighbors pairs representing close neighbor relationships; parameterize the maximum separation in question_ops. Keeps neighbor distance and both endpoint ids.

photoobj_neighbor_denorm.name: photoobj_neighbor_denorm
photoobj_neighbor_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  neighbors AS n
    ON p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_neighbor_denorm.description: Denormalized view joining each photoobj to its neighbor rows (one row per photoobj.objid + neighborobjid) with magnitudes from the photoobj side. Useful to evaluate pairwise color criteria where one side's photometry is in photoobj; can be extended to include neighbor photometry by additional joins.

photoobj_photometry_normalized_50.name: photoobj_photometry_normalized_50
photoobj_photometry_normalized_50.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  NULLIF(p.ra, 'NaN')::double precision AS ra,
  NULLIF(p.dec, 'NaN')::double precision AS dec,
  -- keep raw mags; treat sentinel NULL-like strings/nan as SQL NULL
  NULLIF(p.u, 'NaN')::real AS u,
  NULLIF(p.g, 'NaN')::real AS g,
  NULLIF(p.r, 'NaN')::real AS r,
  NULLIF(p.i, 'NaN')::real AS i,
  NULLIF(p.z, 'NaN')::real AS z
FROM photoobj p
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_photometry_normalized_50.description: Per-photoobj row exposing canonical photometry and sky position with explicit NULL filtering flags removed (keeps raw mags and positions).

neighbors_pairwise.name: neighbors_pairwise
neighbors_pairwise.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  n.type AS type,
  n.neighbortype AS neighbortype,
  n.mode AS mode,
  n.neighbormode AS neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
neighbors_pairwise.description: Pairwise neighbor relationships at the raw neighbor row level; one row per neighbor tuple linking an objid to a neighborobjid with their separation and type flags.

photoobj_with_close_neighbors.name: photoobj_with_close_neighbors
photoobj_with_close_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  neighbors n
  ON p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_with_close_neighbors.description: Denormalized rows of photometric objects joined to their neighbors at the neighbor-pair grain; useful for queries asking about objects with close companions.

photoobj_galaxy_flagged_cohort.name: photoobj_galaxy_flagged_cohort
photoobj_galaxy_flagged_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.value AS "photo_type.value",
  pt.name AS "photo_type.name",
  p.r AS r,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'GALAXY'
photoobj_galaxy_flagged_cohort.description: Subset/cohort of photometric detections that are classified as GALAXY according to the photo_type lookup (keeps original photoobj row per detection).

photoobj_distinct_objects.name: photoobj_distinct_objects
photoobj_distinct_objects.body_sql:
SELECT
  po.objid,
  MIN(po.r) AS min_r,
  MAX(po.r) AS max_r,
  -- first_r: representative r-value chosen from the row with the smallest (run, rerun, field, mode)
  -- lift literals: none needed; tie-breaker uses MIN of composite tuple
  (ARRAY_AGG(po.r ORDER BY po.run, po.rerun, po.field, po.mode, po.objid))[1] AS first_r,
  -- extinction_r_sample: representative extinction_r chosen from same ordering as first_r
  (ARRAY_AGG(po.extinction_r ORDER BY po.run, po.rerun, po.field, po.mode, po.objid))[1] AS extinction_r_sample,
  -- type: representative type chosen from same ordering
  (ARRAY_AGG(po.type ORDER BY po.run, po.rerun, po.field, po.mode, po.objid))[1] AS type
FROM
  photoobj_photometry_normalized po
GROUP BY
  po.objid
photoobj_distinct_objects.description: One row per distinct photometric object (objid) with representative photometry; useful to count distinct objects matching photometric criteria.

photo_type_lookup_55.name: photo_type_lookup_55
photo_type_lookup_55.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name,
  pt.description
FROM photo_type AS pt
ORDER BY pt.value
photo_type_lookup_55.description: Lookup table mapping photo type integer codes to human-readable names and descriptions.

photoobj_with_spectroscopic_flag.name: photoobj_with_spectroscopic_flag
photoobj_with_spectroscopic_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.r AS r,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,
  p.type AS type,
  (CASE WHEN g.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END) AS is_linked_to_galspecline
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  galspecline g
ON
  p.objid = g.specobjid
photoobj_with_spectroscopic_flag.description: Denormalized photoobj rows annotated with whether they are linked to a spectroscopic object via galspecline (i.e., photoobj.objid = galspecline.specobjid).

photoobj_base.name: photoobj_base
photoobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.u      AS u,
  p.g      AS g,
  p.r      AS r,
  p.i      AS i,
  p.z      AS z,
  p.ra     AS ra,
  p.dec    AS dec,
  p.type   AS type
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_base.description: Canonical normalized projection of photoobj photometric measurements and positional identifiers, with raw flux/magnitude columns exposed for filtering and sorting.

photo_type_lookup_58.name: photo_type_lookup_58
photo_type_lookup_58.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM
  photo_type pt
photo_type_lookup_58.description: Lookup mapping of photo type numeric code to its name and description, useful for resolving type codes (e.g., 'GALAXY').

photoobj_with_type_name.name: photoobj_with_type_name
photoobj_with_type_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS type_name
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name.description: Denormalized photoobj rows augmented with the human-readable type name from photo_type for easy filtering by semantic type (e.g., GALAXY).

photo_type_lookup_60.name: photo_type_lookup_60
photo_type_lookup_60.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM
  photo_type pt
photo_type_lookup_60.description: Lookup of photo object type codes to their textual name/description (maps photoobj.type -> human-readable type). Useful for selecting object classes such as GALAXY, STAR, etc.

photoobj_basic_astrometry_and_mags.name: photoobj_basic_astrometry_and_mags
photoobj_basic_astrometry_and_mags.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_basic_astrometry_and_mags.description: Normalized projection of photoobj exposing id, astrometry (ra, dec), and the five-band magnitudes and relevant metadata. Nulls are preserved so downstream filters can require non-null magnitudes. Useful as the canonical photometric object row for selection and joins.

photoobj_color_indices.name: photoobj_color_indices
photoobj_color_indices.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  -- lift any literals out: no literals needed for calculations here
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_color_indices.description: Compute common color indices (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) per photometric object to simplify color-based selections. This is row-level (one row per photoobj.objid) and not aggregated across objects.

photoobj_star_candidate_cohort.name: photoobj_star_candidate_cohort
photoobj_star_candidate_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- color columns computed as differences; lift literals (none) out of view
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z
FROM
  photoobj_star_cohort AS p
WHERE
  -- require magnitude values to be finite (not null) for all five bands
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  -- optional: exclude objects with non-finite ra/dec
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- configurable magnitude/color bounds are intentionally NOT hard-coded here;
  -- view returns candidates passing basic validity so question_ops can apply numeric thresholds
photoobj_star_candidate_cohort.description: Cohort view selecting photoobj rows that are potential stellar sources based on magnitude validity and configurable magnitude/color bounds. This view should be used as the base for final question-specific filters (numerical thresholds placed in question_ops).

photoobj_star_cohort_64.name: photoobj_star_cohort_64
photoobj_star_cohort_64.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- lift literals OUT: none here; use columns directly
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
WHERE
  -- require detections in all five bands (non-null mags)
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  -- basic photometric quality: clean flag set to 1 (lifted literal)
  AND p.clean = 1
  -- ensure cmodel magnitudes and centroid positions are present
  AND p.cmodelmag_u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.cmodelmag_g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.cmodelmag_r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.rowc IS NOT NULL
  AND p.colc IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_cohort_64.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections (photoobj) with non-null magnitudes and basic photometric quality columns exposed. Useful as the base set of observable objects for color/magnitude selection.

photoobj_spatial_and_image_centroid.name: photoobj_spatial_and_image_centroid
photoobj_spatial_and_image_centroid.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  -- canonical sky positions as double precision
  COALESCE(NULLIF(p.ra, 'NaN'::double precision), 0.0::double precision) AS ra,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(p.dec, 'NaN'::double precision), 0.0::double precision) AS dec,
  -- image centroid cast to real for compactness, preserve NULL if unknown
  (CASE WHEN p.rowc IS NOT NULL THEN p.rowc::real ELSE NULL END) AS rowc,
  (CASE WHEN p.colc IS NOT NULL THEN p.colc::real ELSE NULL END) AS colc,
  -- canonical run/rerun/field as integers (smallint range)
  p.run::integer AS run,
  p.rerun::integer AS rerun,
  p.field::integer AS field
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_spatial_and_image_centroid.description: Canonicalized spatial and image-centroid measures for each photoobj, exposing RA/DEC and pixel centroid (rowc,colc) and commonly used photometry columns; casts/normalizes types where useful for downstream filters.

photoobj_photometry_summary.name: photoobj_photometry_summary
photoobj_photometry_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- photometric magnitudes (lifted literals: none)
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- cmodel magnitudes (may be null)
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  -- type and clean flags for selection / color cuts
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_photometry_summary.description: Per-photoobj photometric magnitudes and cmodel magnitudes (u,g,r,i,z and cmodelmag_u/g/r) with no aggregation, exposing these measures for color cuts and null-exclusion logic.

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  -- canonical coords: prefer cleaned photometry normalized ra/dec, fall back to core if null
  COALESCE(p.ra, pc.ra)::double precision AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, pc.dec)::double precision AS dec,
  -- magnitudes: prefer normalized photometry columns; null-cleaning: NULL stays NULL (no sentinel)
  -- lift literals: none needed here; just pass through and cast to double precision
  p.u::double precision AS u,
  p.g::double precision AS g,
  p.r::double precision AS r,
  -- type: canonical integer type from photoobj_core if available, else from photometry table
  COALESCE(pc.type, p.type)::integer AS type
FROM
  photoobj_photometry_normalized p
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj_core pc
ON
  p.objid = pc.objid
photoobj_basic_photometry.description: Canonical per-photo-object photometry and positional columns with null-cleaning and canonical numeric types. One row per photoobj.objid exposing magnitudes and coords for downstream filtering.

photo_type_lookup_68.name: photo_type_lookup_68
photo_type_lookup_68.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM photo_type
photo_type_lookup_68.description: Mapping of photo type code values to human-readable names and descriptions. Useful to join against photoobj.type to filter or label object classes (e.g., GALAXY).

photoobj_position_and_type_cohort.name: photoobj_position_and_type_cohort
photoobj_position_and_type_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type
FROM
  photoobj p
WHERE
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
photoobj_position_and_type_cohort.description: A reusable cohort view selecting photoobj rows that have non-null id and coordinates; exposes keys and spatial columns for spatial/filtering queries.

photoobj_canonical_photometry.name: photoobj_canonical_photometry
photoobj_canonical_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  -- lift any literals out of view: no literals here
  -- ensure numeric photometry usable in arithmetic: cast to double precision
  p.u::double precision AS u,
  p.g::double precision AS g,
  p.r::double precision AS r,
  -- preserve cmodel mags; cast to double precision so downstream math works
  p.cmodelmag_u::double precision AS cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g::double precision AS cmodelmag_g,
  -- preserve clean as integer (keep NULLs)
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.type::integer AS type
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_canonical_photometry.description: Normalized photometry and coordinates for photoobj rows: exposes canonical numeric photometric columns and handles any necessary casting/NULL retention so downstream filters can use arithmetic (e.g., u - g).

photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.name: photoobj_with_neighbor_counts
photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  COALESCE(nc.neighbor_count, 0) AS neighbor_count
FROM
  photoobj_core p
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT COUNT(*)::integer AS neighbor_count
  FROM neighbors n
  WHERE n.objid = p.objid
    AND n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL
    -- distance threshold lifted out as literal: 60.0 arcsec (example)
    AND n.distance <= 60.0
) nc ON true
photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.description: Photometric objects augmented with count of neighbors within specified distance — useful for isolation/companionship filters and deblending-aware selections.

spectroscopic_objects_core.name: spectroscopic_objects_core
spectroscopic_objects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  -- choose bestobjid when present, otherwise fall back to specobjid match to photoobj.objid
  COALESCE(s.bestobjid::bigint, p.objid) AS objid,
  -- prefer coordinates from matched photoobj if available, otherwise specobj ra/dec
  COALESCE(p.ra, s.ra) AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, s.dec) AS dec,
  -- prefer g magnitude from photoobj if available
  COALESCE(p.g, NULL) AS g,
  s.z AS z,
  s.class AS class
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON (p.objid = COALESCE(s.bestobjid::bigint, s.specobjid::bigint))
WHERE s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
spectroscopic_objects_core.description: Denormalized one-row-per-spectroscopic-object linking specobj to its photometric best/primary photometry (photoobj) when available, exposing key classification and redshift alongside photo magnitudes and coordinates. Prefer bestobjid when present but also include direct specobjid match.

spectroscopic_classification.name: spectroscopic_classification
spectroscopic_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.zwarning
FROM specobj s
spectroscopic_classification.description: Spectroscopic classification and redshift attributes per spectroscopic observation, for building cohorts by class and redshift cuts.

photoobj_basic_photometry_74.name: photoobj_basic_photometry_74
photoobj_basic_photometry_74.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- canonical band magnitudes: prefer normalized photometry cmodel where available,
  -- fall back to base u/g/r/i/z from photoobj if cmodel columns are NULL.
  COALESCE(p.cmodelmag_g, p.g) AS g,
  COALESCE(p.cmodelmag_r, p.r) AS r,
  COALESCE(p.cmodelmag_u, p.u) AS u,
  COALESCE(p.i, p.i) AS i,
  COALESCE(p.z, p.z) AS z,
  p.run,
  p.field,
  p.rerun,
  p.mode
FROM photoobj_photometry_normalized p
photoobj_basic_photometry_74.description: One row per detected photometric object with canonical positional and band magnitudes (no filtering); useful as the primary photometric entity for joins and magnitude/radius-based filters.

specobj_primary_spectra.name: specobj_primary_spectra
specobj_primary_spectra.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid,
  s.scienceprimary
FROM specobj s
WHERE s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
specobj_primary_spectra.description: One row per spectroscopic object (spectrum) with primary classification and redshift info; use to filter/classify objects by spectroscopic properties.

photoobj_with_best_spec.name: photoobj_with_best_spec
photoobj_with_best_spec.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.g,
  s.specobjid,
  s.class,
  s.z
FROM
  photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  /* find the best specobj matching this photoobj, if any */
  SELECT s2.specobjid, s2.class, s2.z
  FROM specobj AS s2
  WHERE s2.bestobjid = p.objid
  ORDER BY s2.specobjid NULLS LAST
  LIMIT 1
) AS s ON true
photoobj_with_best_spec.description: Denormalized view linking photometric objects to their best matching spectroscopic record (if any). One row per photometric object with spectroscopic fields from specobj when present. Useful for queries that need photometry together with spectrum-based classification and redshift.
